issues.legal_issue: Emergency requisition powers for maintaining essential supplies and services cannot be used to provide a commercial facility whose absence would not deprive the community of essential supplies or services.
material_facts: The property was requisitioned so a corporation could build shops and showrooms to display and sell handloom goods made by rural weavers.
The stated objective was to help weavers find a market for their goods; the community could continue to exist without the showroom and would not thereby lose essential supplies or services.
issues.conclusion: The purpose of the requisition had no nexus with maintaining supplies and services essential to the life of the community, so the order was ultra vires and unauthorised.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1) permits requisition for maintaining supplies and services essential to the life of the community only where, without the requisition, the community would be deprived of those essential supplies or services. The Court distinguished Parvej Aktar v. Union of India, which concerned protections for the handloom industry under a different statute and did not establish that a showroom could be requisitioned under Section 23(1).

predicates.challenge_to_emergency_property_requisit: A party challenges an authority's use of emergency powers to requisition property.
predicates.requisition_purpose_is_marketing_facilit: The authority requisitions property to provide a facility for marketing or displaying goods.
predicates.community_not_deprived_without_facility: The community would not lose essential supplies or services if the facility were not provided.

issues.definition: When an emergency property requisition is challenged, its use to provide a marketing facility exceeds the emergency power if the community would not lose essential supplies or services without that facility.

issues.legal_issue: Emergency requisition powers are limited to emergent needs and cannot be used to meet a permanent purpose.
material_facts: The requisition was made under an Act enacted for emergency situations.
The land was intended for shops and showrooms that would serve an ongoing purpose, rather than a temporary emergency need.

The governing provision limited the duration of requisition to the period for which the property was required for its specified purposes, and the Act provided for acquisition in certain circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The emergency requisition power could not be used for the permanent purpose of providing the showroom, and requisition orders under the Act had to be of limited duration commensurate with the emergent need.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 23(1) and 23(3) of the Defence and Internal Security of India Act, 1971 confine requisition to specified emergency purposes and to the period for which the property is required for those purposes; Section 30 provides for acquisition in specified circumstances. The Court distinguished Grahak Sanstha Manch v. State of Maharashtra, which interpreted a different statute and held that a permanent public purpose could support requisition there, while still recognising that requisition cannot continue indefinitely. It also relied on M/s. Speedcrafts Pvt. Ltd. v. The District Magistrate for the view that requisition under these provisions is unavailable for a non-temporary public purpose.

predicates.challenge_to_emergency_property_requisit: A party challenges an authority's use of emergency powers to requisition property.
predicates.requisition_power_arises_from_emergency_: The authority relies on a law that grants requisition powers for emergency purposes.
predicates.purpose_is_permanent: The property is required for an ongoing purpose rather than for a limited emergent need.

issues.definition: A permanent purpose cannot be pursued by emergency requisition when the challenged power comes from a law granting requisition powers for emergency purposes.

issues.legal_issue: A person with a subsisting leasehold interest in requisitioned property has standing to challenge the requisition.
material_facts: The claimants had acquired the original lessee's interest in the land, and the leases allowed renewal at the lessee's option up to a maximum term.
The leases were current when the requisition order was made, and there was no evidence that renewal had been refused or that the leases had been terminated or the land resumed.
The authorities had demanded and received rent for the land from the claimants.
issues.conclusion: The claimants had sufficient locus standi to challenge the requisition order and seek restoration of their leasehold rights and possession.
issues.legal_principle: A person whose subsisting proprietary or leasehold interest is affected by a requisition has standing to challenge it. The Court assessed the claimants' interest as it existed when the order was made, noting the transferable leasehold interest, the renewal options, the absence of evidence of termination or refusal of renewal, and the collection of rent.

predicates.challenge_to_property_requisition: A person challenges an authority's requisition of property in which that person claims an interest.
predicates.claimant_succeeded_to_leasehold_interest: The claimant acquired the leasehold interest from the original lessee.
predicates.leasehold_interest_was_subsisting_when_r: The leasehold interest remained in force when the authority made the requisition, with no established termination or refusal of renewal.

issues.definition: A claimant who acquired a leasehold interest that was still subsisting when property was requisitioned has standing to challenge that requisition.

issues.legal_issue: An emergency requisition cannot be continued indefinitely after the emergency and the underlying need have ended, even if the law authorising it has expired with a saving clause.
material_facts: The order was made during an emergency under a temporary Act, and the emergency and the Act had since ended.
The requisition continued for more than two decades, although its original purpose had become obsolete.
The authorities had not acquired the property under the statutory acquisition procedure.
issues.conclusion: The continued requisition had become unreasonable, amounted to an abuse and colourable exercise of power, and could no longer be sustained; the saving clause did not prevent the Court from examining the order's validity or continued operation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 1(3) preserves the previous operation of the Act and things duly done under it, but does not prevent scrutiny of whether an order was validly made or whether its continued operation is lawful. Section 23(3) limits requisition to the period of the relevant need. Under Grahak Sanstha Manch v. State of Maharashtra, a requisition cannot continue indefinitely and must last only a reasonable period, assessed in the circumstances of the case. The Court also considered the emergency character of the Act and the acquisition mechanism in Section 30.

predicates.challenge_to_emergency_property_requisit: A party challenges an authority's use of emergency powers to requisition property.
predicates.emergency_and_authorising_law_have_ended: The emergency has ceased and the temporary law that authorised the requisition has expired.
predicates.requisition_continues_long_after_need_en: The authority continues to hold the property for a prolonged period after the original need has become obsolete.

issues.definition: A continued requisition is unreasonable and unsustainable when it is challenged after the emergency and authorising law have ended and the authority keeps the property long after the original need has become obsolete.
